svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Figure 1. Stateful tracking compared with stateless tracking
svg.desc: Two panels. The left panel is stateful tracking, which stores something on your device: cookies, local storage, indexed database, and cache entries. You can delete it and the browser can partition it. The right panel is stateless tracking, which measures something about your device: canvas rendering, graphics vendor, fonts, audio processing, and screen geometry. You cannot delete it and it survives private browsing. A band below states that pressure on the stateful side moved the work to the stateless side, with measured figures for canvas fingerprinting growth.
svg.text: One family stores something on your device. The other measures something about it. Only one of them can be deleted.

g.text: First-party and third-party cookies
Local storage and session storage
Indexed database entries
Cache entries and ETag values
Service worker storage
What is true of all of it
You can delete it, and deleting it works.
The browser can partition it, so one site cannot read
what another site stored.
You can see it in the developer tools, today, yourself.

svg.text: Third-party cookies are blocked by default in Safari, Firefox

g.text: Canvas rendering hash
Graphics vendor and renderer strings
Installed font list
Audio processing signature
Screen geometry, time zone, language, core count
What is true of all of it
You cannot delete it. There is nothing stored to delete.
It survives a cookie clear, and it survives private
browsing, because neither one changes your hardware.
You cannot see it happen. It takes milliseconds.

svg.text: Measured canvas fingerprinting: 1.6% of the top 1M sites in
2016, and 12.7% of the top 20K sites in 2025.
Pressure on the left side moved the work to the right side.
This is the most important fact in this lesson. As browsers restricted what could be stored, the industry shifted to what could be measured, and the measured
kind is the kind that you cannot clear. See References 4 to 7.
